dropped.checklist_item: - [ ] Make transition_ticket_start (and the daemon it starts) refuse new work while the InFlightGauge is draining, the same way transition_ticket does via gauge.admit / DRAINED_TOOLS.
evidence: Shared resource: InFlightGauge state `self._draining` / `self._value`, guarded by `self._lock` (src/rebar/_mcp_health.py:83-86).
Executor 1 (signal handler): `def _on_sigterm(...): gauge.begin_draining(); deadline = time.monotonic() + grace_seconds` then `drain_then_exit(...)` (src/rebar/_mcp_serving.py:89-104).

Executor 2: a transition_ticket_start call on the serving thread runs `anyio.to_thread.run_sync(lambda: _start_gate_job(...))` (src/rebar/_mcp_ticket_async.py:79-91). _start_gate_job then calls `_spawn_gate_daemon` -> `spawn_context_daemon(_bg, ...)` (src/rebar/_mcp_llm.py:254,296).

Sibling accessor and its guard: transition_ticket is in `SIGNING_TOOLS = frozenset({"transition_ticket", "sign_manifest", "sign_review"})` (src/rebar/_mcp_health.py:38). Its wrapper calls `gauge.admit`, which runs `with self._lock: if self._draining: raise MCPRetiringError(...)` (src/rebar/_mcp_health.py:122-133). Only names in DRAINED_TOOLS get that wrapper: `for name in sorted(DRAINED_TOOLS): ... tool.fn = _wrap_tool_fn(tool.fn, gauge, name)` (src/rebar/_mcp_health.py:193-204).

The new accessor has no guard. transition_ticket_start is not in DRAINED_TOOLS (src/rebar/_mcp_health.py:34,38,45). Its daemon is counted only through `hold()`, which by its own docstring 'never refuses while draining' (src/rebar/_mcp_health.py:113-120; spawn_context_daemon line 124-125: `hold = _WORK_HOLD.get(); release = hold() if hold is not None else _no_release`). The inner `sync(**arguments)` is a fresh `make_tool(spec, ctx)` function (src/rebar/_mcp_ticket_async.py:114) with no gauge tracking (`gauge` does not appear in src/rebar/_mcp_derive.py), so it never reaches admit().

Interleaving: the SIGTERM handler writes `self._draining = True` (src/rebar/_mcp_health.py:103). A later transition_ticket_start never reads `_draining`, increments `_value` through hold(), and starts the close. Meanwhile the drain loop `while gauge.value > 0 and monotonic() < deadline` (src/rebar/_mcp_serving.py:46) is counting down a deadline fixed at SIGTERM time.

Harm: a close accepted late in the window can still be running when the deadline expires and the process exits or is killed. It is then cut off between its STATUS commit and its completion-certificate signature, leaving the ticket closed but uncertified. SIGNING_TOOLS exists to prevent this (docstring: 'Retirement cut a close off between its STATUS commit and its signature, leaving it closed and uncertified like a forced close (bug external-taxonomic-iguanodon)', src/rebar/_mcp_health.py:38-43). New intake also keeps the gauge above 0, which the MCPRetiringError docstring says refusal is meant to prevent (src/rebar/_mcp_health.py:66-72).

Note: review_code_start likewise skips the admit() check that review_code (CERTIFIED_TOOLS, src/rebar/_mcp_health.py:34) gets. review_plan_start and verify_completion_start already behave this way, and the extra drain time is load-only, so that part is deferred to performance.
dropped.finding: transition_ticket_start skips the shutdown check that refuses transition_ticket once a SIGTERM drain has begun, so a retiring container still accepts and starts a gated close.
scenarios: Blue-green retirement: SIGTERM arrives, draining starts, an agent re-fires transition_ticket_start for a close. The retiring container accepts it instead of returning MCPRetiringError, and the close runs a minutes-long completion gate against a fixed grace deadline.
The grace or container stop timeout expires while the daemon sits between the status commit and the certificate signature.
dropped.suggested_fix: Put the starter through the same admission check as its sync twin. For example, add `transition_ticket_start` to SIGNING_TOOLS / DRAINED_TOOLS and give async starters an async-aware admit wrapper, since instrument_certified_tools only wraps sync bodies and fails loudly on async ones. Alternatively, call `gauge.admit("transition_ticket")` before `_start_gate_job`, so a draining container raises MCPRetiringError instead of starting the close.

dropped.checklist_item: - [ ] Keep the code-review degrade disposition (coverage.retryable / resolution_class) in the review_code_start run record and gate_status, and do not report a retryable INDETERMINATE degrade as a plain 'passed'.
evidence: Primary failure: a provider outage mid-review becomes the degrade verdict built at src/rebar/llm/workflow/gate_dispatch.py:343-353: {"verdict": "INDETERMINATE", coverage: {..., **_failure.resolution_fields(outcome)}}. That puts retryable/resolution_class on coverage. It is returned, not raised, so _review_code_body's `except LLMError` (src/rebar/_mcp_llm.py:137-140) never runs.

The shim copies coverage to the top level so the classifier can map a retryable outage to exit 11 (src/rebar/llm/code_review/shim.py:91-94). The CLI branches on it with `if coverage.get("retryable"):` (src/rebar/_cli/_llm_commands.py:124).
Old surfaced disposition (sync review_code, still current): the full review_result with coverage.retryable=True and resolution_class, so the caller can retry.

New surfaced disposition (review_code_start, which AGENTS.md now recommends): _terminal_from_result sees no top-level 'error', unwraps the nested verdict dict (src/rebar/_mcp_llm.py:195-200) and returns ("passed", "INDETERMINATE"). _spawn_gate_daemon records only status/verdict/error (src/rebar/_mcp_llm.py:239-248). _gate_sidecar_fields returns {} for gate types other than plan_review/verify_completion (src/rebar/_mcp_llm.py:204-205).

gate_run_status returns only job_id/status/ticket_id/gate_type/verdict/error (src/rebar/llm/gate_runs.py:358-367). Because review_code_start passes ticket_id "" (src/rebar/_mcp_llm.py:424), the durable/findings branch is skipped (src/rebar/llm/gate_runs.py:370). _durable_verdict also returns None for code_review (src/rebar/llm/gate_runs.py:128-129). Nothing on the poll path carries retryable.

The starter docstring tells pollers that `passed` means `verdict` is the gate's PASS/BLOCK (src/rebar/_mcp_llm.py:408-409). A poller acting on that sees a settled 'passed' run, not a transient outage to retry.
dropped.finding: review_code_start reports a retryable code-review provider outage as status 'passed' with verdict 'INDETERMINATE' and drops coverage.retryable and resolution_class. The sync review_code returns that disposition and the CLI classifier uses it to choose exit 11.
scenarios: A provider throttle during review_code_start: gate_status shows {status: 'passed', verdict: 'INDETERMINATE'} with no retryable flag. The agent treats the review as done or inconclusive and does not re-run it, where review_code would have returned coverage.retryable=true.
dropped.suggested_fix: In _gate_sidecar_fields (or a code_review-specific branch), copy result['coverage'] retryable/resolution_class/diagnostic into the run record and pass them through in gate_run_status. Optionally have _terminal_from_result return 'failed' (or keep the retryable flag) when the nested verdict is INDETERMINATE and coverage.llm_ran is False.

dropped.checklist_item: - [ ] Store the raised exception's structured envelope (error_code_for(exc), exit_code/returncode, and LLM outcome retryable/resolution_class if present) in the transition_ticket_start run record and pass it through in gate_status, so a retryable close failure (exit 11) or concurrency mismatch (exit 10) is distinct from a permanent refusal.
evidence: Primary failure: a retryable provider/runtime outage in the close verifier raises CommandError(returncode=11) (src/rebar/_commands/completion_verifier_run.py:41, 60-65). rebar.transition rewraps it as RebarError(returncode=exc.returncode) (src/rebar/_lib_writes.py:358-363). A stale current_status raises ConcurrencyError(returncode=10) (src/rebar/_lib_writes.py:352-357).

Old surfaced disposition (sync transition_ticket): the MCP guard turns RebarError/CommandError into McpEnvelopeError(error_envelope(error_code_for(exc), '', str(exc), returncode)) (src/rebar/_mcp_errors.py:69-73). The envelope keeps a typed 'error' code and an integer 'exit_code' (src/rebar/_engine_support/output.py:141-143), so a client can branch on exit_code 11 to retry or 10 to re-read and retry.

New surfaced disposition (transition_ticket_start): _spawn_gate_daemon catches every exception as `error, verdict = exc, str(exc)` and records status 'failed', verdict str(exc), error str(exc) (src/rebar/_mcp_llm.py:236-245). handle.complete gets the exception object, but the async poller never reads it. gate_run_status returns only status/verdict/error strings (src/rebar/llm/gate_runs.py:357-367).

As a result, a retryable verifier outage, a concurrency mismatch, a permanent completion FAIL refusal, and a stale daemon ('daemon-stopped', src/rebar/llm/gate_runs.py:317-323) all show up as the same untyped `failed` + prose. The only trace left is an '(exit N)' substring in the RebarError message, and the ConcurrencyError message does not include one.

The new docs tell callers that `failed` 'carries the refusal in error' (src/rebar/_mcp_ticket_async.py docstring / AGENTS.md hunk). That frames every failure as a refusal, so a client is pushed to give up on a close that should be retried.
dropped.finding: transition_ticket_start turns a refused close into an untyped string. The sync tool's structured envelope keeps the exit code (11 = transient verifier outage, retry; 10 = concurrency mismatch; 1 = fail-closed) and the error code. The async record keeps only str(exc), so a poller can't tell a retryable verifier outage from a permanent gate refusal.
scenarios: A throttled completion verifier during a close started through transition_ticket_start: gate_status shows {status: 'failed', error: 'rebar transition failed (exit 11): ...'} with no exit_code or error-code field. A client that branched on envelope.exit_code == 11 to retry now sees a generic failure and stops.
